outcome: maternal complications (preterm labor, preeclampsia, antepartum hemorrhage, postpartum hemorrhage, abruptio placentae, IUGR, sepsis, placenta previa)
neonatal complications (NICU admission, prematurity, respiratory distress, meconium-stained liquor, intrauterine fetal demise)
cohort: 190 pregnant women with severe anemia delivering at a tertiary care hospital in Southeast Rajasthan, India.
finding: Severe anemia in pregnancy significantly increases the risk of maternal and neonatal complications during labor and delivery, with LSCS being the commonest mode of delivery in this cohort.
mod_finding: LSCS was the most common mode of delivery (58.4%) among women with severe anemia.
